parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized exact C++ behavior, std::stoi-style permissive parsing, default n=11, wrapping i32 arithmetic, Cargo plus root test11.rs, no crates, and byte-identical stdout.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but spawned probe_binary for runtime behavior and later review_port for inspection. The child also independently wrote implementation files, creating overlapping deliverable ownership.
parallel.implementation: The parent first wrote an Rc-backed PersistentVector that cloned on append, noticed the large-case comparison was too slow, changed append to mutate owned Vec storage, and the child-provided final module split also used an efficient Vector::push_back(mut self).
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent detected that /output had been rewritten into the child's module split, inspected the current files, accepted the current state after rebuilding, and produced /output/test11 plus Cargo artifacts.
parallel.verification: The run compared default, zero, negative, numeric-prefix, overflow, invalid, and out-of-range cases; review_port also checked normal and error cases; the official evaluator later passed all 38 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The retained issue is not final functional failure but an adverse shared-state episode: child writes replaced the required entry/project files and forced parent reconciliation before closure.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same prompt obligations, including root test11.rs, std::env::args, std-only code, permissive stoi behavior, wrapping arithmetic, and Cargo/direct-rustc builds.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run had one implementation owner and one local plan: probe reference behavior, write modular Cargo files, build, fix issues, test selected cases, and finish.
serial.implementation: The serial code implemented parsing and wrapping arithmetic but left PersistentVector::push_back taking &self and cloning the whole Vec on each append, making vector construction quadratic.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote one coherent Cargo project, fixed a crate-path import from crate:: to super::, built with Cargo and direct rustc, and delivered the expected executable locations.
serial.verification: The serial run checked default, zero, four, 12abc, negative, 65536, invalid, and out-of-range cases and reported matching stderr/status for parse failures, but those checks did not expose the hidden-case failure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluator failed 6 of 38 tests; the visible code difference most consistent with that discordance is the serial O(n^2) append path that the parallel run corrected.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact porting obligations and explicitly isolated stoi prefix parsing, negative inputs, overflow wrapping, project layout, and direct rustc/Cargo requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations and probed prefix parsing, whitespace/sign handling, invalid/out-of-range exceptions, and overflow boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the difference was not a missed prompt item but how far each run pursued performance-sensitive faithful behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated runtime probing and review while also implementing locally; probe_binary went beyond probing and wrote its own project into the same output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all probing, implementation, fixes, verification, and closure in one local owner without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained additional implementation/review exploration but introduced overlapping ownership of the deliverable tree; serial avoided coordination risk but had less independent correction pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child had the task prompt and acted in the same /output workspace, but there was no visible isolation or ownership contract preventing it from replacing the parent-owned entry/project files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interface boundary; the local code and project layout were internally consistent after the import fix.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's missing workspace contract manifested as competing writes, not as a missing task requirement; serial's single-owner context avoided that interface risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel moved from a cloning PersistentVector to owned mutable push_back, and the final child module split used Vector::push_back(mut self) plus wrapping math and stoi-style parsing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented parsing and wrapping math but retained PersistentVector::push_back(&self) that clones the entire backing vector for every append.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final parallel artifact avoids quadratic vector construction; the serial artifact keeps the quadratic append path and is the one that failed hidden official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on children, timed out, interrupted both active children, and then inspected the shared output tree rather than receiving a normal final child handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its local implementation progressed through build failure, fix, rebuild, selected verification, and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's child lifecycle was messy but recovered through artifact inspection; serial had simpler lifecycle but did not acquire the same performance correction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent and child wrote overlapping /output project files; the child replaced the required test11.rs and module graph, and the parent later noticed the project changed underneath it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one project tree, fixed one local import, and rebuilt without any competing writer or shared-workspace provenance problem.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state collision that required reconciliation; serial avoided the collision but its final source retained the performance defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel rebuilt after reconciliation, verified default/0/4/-1/12abc/65536 plus invalid and out-of-range cases, and official evaluation passed all 38 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified selected normal and error cases including 65536, but official evaluation completed with only 32 of 38 tests passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both local verification sets were plausible smoke checks; official acceptance distinguishes them, and the visible code difference points to serial hidden performance gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and many more tokens with subagents, waits, interrupts, and reconciliation, but still closed within budget and passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with no subagents and no timeout, but closed with a final artifact that failed six official cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget overhead produced one adverse shared-state episode but also surfaced/landed a performance-safe implementation; serial used less budget but closed with an uncorrected performance risk.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Parallel passed all official tests while serial failed six. The visible task-solving difference is implementation performance: parallel identified the first clone-on-append vector as too slow and ended with an efficient owned-Vec append path, while serial retained a PersistentVector append that cloned the entire vector every time. The pair does not expose per-test failure names, so this is a supported comparative explanation rather than an exclusive root-cause claim.
parallel_contributors: Parallel explicitly noticed the initial immutable-vector wrapper was too slow during large-case verification and patched push_back to mutate owned storage.
The final parallel project used the child module split with Vector::push_back(mut self), wrapping arithmetic, and stoi-style parsing, then rebuilt and verified the current tree.
serial_contributors: Serial implemented correct-looking parsing and wrapping behavior for selected probes but kept an O(n^2) clone-on-append PersistentVector.
Serial local verification passed smoke cases including 65536, but the official evaluator still failed 6 of 38 cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's final vector construction clones the whole backing Vec on every push_back; parallel's final vector construction appends into owned Vec storage.
Parallel performed an extra large-input performance correction after a long-running comparison; serial did not perform that optimization.
evaluator_effects: The isolated pair contains only evaluator summaries, not detailed failing-case logs, so hidden-case attribution is inferred from code and trajectory evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

The workspace was shared, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven for the same write episode.

retained_patterns.reason: A child replaced the parent-owned required entry/project files in /output while the parent still owned the final deliverable, and the parent then had to inspect and rebuild the changed tree. The pattern is adverse coordination overhead, not the explanation for the discordant outcome, because parallel ultimately passed.

retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The source tree was affected, but the directly executed and submitted entry source /output/test11.rs was part of the overwrite, making Deliverable Overwrite more specific.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: The parent/child writes to Cargo.toml, test11.rs, and module files are treated as one deliverable-overwrite episode rather than separate per-file labels.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Final-Tree Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes are suppressed because Deliverable Overwrite is the most specific label for the same write chain.

Early Child Termination and Missing Implementation Join are suppressed because the interruption and inspection steps were downstream of the same shared-state episode and did not create a separate unfinished-result consequence.
